correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southern opening and northeastern upper channel
correspondence.finding: The poster depicts the selected southern opening on a narrow channel south of Kaskatamagan Sipi Wildlife Management Area. Its first short northward and northeastward intervals, including the joins between the four parts, follow the same mapped channel. No adjacent lake or separate tributary label is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Long eastern upper arc and turn back west
correspondence.finding: The selected course follows the mapped channel northeast toward the eastern tip of Kaskatamagan Sipi Wildlife Management Area, then rounds its eastward bend and turns west. The nearby longer north-going channel farther east is separate. The source provides ordinary continuity through this lowland passage but no selected-channel hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward short joins inside the wildlife management area
correspondence.finding: Both short westward selected parts correspond to the continuous mapped channel inside the eastern portion of the wildlife management area. The source shows the connected westward bend, rather than a transfer to the separate major channel farther west.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward exit from the wildlife management area
correspondence.finding: The selected west-to-north bend follows the same mapped river out of the wildlife management area. The larger west-side drainage remains distinct. The source depicts an uninterrupted channel; no named lake, reservoir or managed transfer is identified on this selected passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Central northwest-going river and intermediate joins
correspondence.finding: The long selected northwestern reach and three short succeeding joins correspond to the mapped bend sequence and side-tributary setting. Ecoregion boundary symbols cross part of this interval, but the channel is visible on both sides and its ordinary continuation is identifiable. No branch name or conservation-area name is promoted to a river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower northwest-going approach
correspondence.finding: The selected lower approach follows the mapped river toward the coastal strip east of the Hayes River outlet. It remains distinct from the Hayes corridor and the other coastal streams farther east. Conservation boundaries partly overprint the river but do not introduce a different route.

correspondence.component_scope: Final north-going reach and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The final selected part follows the north-going river to the Hudson Bay coastal outlet east of Hayes. The map supports the river-to-coast termination at ordinary outlet scale. Thick coastal ecoregion and conservation-boundary symbols obscure precise mouth branches and shoreline details; exact present banks or tidal conditions are not claimed.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and West Navidad River
correspondence.finding: The chosen northwestern opening is on the mapped headward channel west of Freyburg. Its connected southeastward route is repeatedly labelled West Navidad River and passes west of Schulenburg, across Interstate 10 and U.S. 90, then east toward Oakland. The source shows the initial channel and intermediate feeder joins, including the Mulberry Creek approach. Straight modeled segments locally cut small meanders and floodplain bends. The chosen opening is not asserted as the ultimate natural source.

correspondence.component_scope: West and East Navidad junction near Oakland
correspondence.finding: East Navidad River approaches from the northeast and joins West Navidad River near Oakland. The combined river turns south and is labelled Navidad River. The original visibly establishes this junction and the selected transition; the two upstream branch names remain distinct.

correspondence.component_scope: Navidad River through Hackberry and Sublime
correspondence.finding: A continuous named channel extends south from the branch junction through the Hackberry vicinity and past Sublime. Big Rocky Creek, Honey Creek and other smaller feeders join the selected corridor. The repeated river labels, connected bends and overlapping maps cover all selected intervening parts and the U.S. 90A crossing.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Navidad corridor through Vienna, Seclusion and Speaks
correspondence.finding: The maps show Navidad River continuing southeast past Vienna and Seclusion before bending southwest below Speaks and turning south into Jackson County. Mapped tributary junctions and continuous meanders cover the selected route through the wooded plain. Surrounding ponds and wetlands are lateral settings; no separate through-pond transfer is needed.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Navidad River and entry to Lake Texana
correspondence.finding: The named Navidad corridor passes Morales and Mount Olive, turns east, and enters the northwestern arm of Lake Texana near the Sandy Creek approach and U.S. 59 crossing. The original shows the connected river-to-reservoir transition, including wetland-bordered meanders and the inlet. Nearby drainage canals are not substituted for the selected river.

correspondence.component_scope: Lake Texana passage and dam/outlet connection
correspondence.finding: The selected route crosses the connected main body of Lake Texana from its northern Navidad arm to the southern dam. A mapped outlet at the southwestern end leads into the separately labelled lower Navidad River. The reservoir profile independently places Lake Texana, also called Palmetto Bend Dam and Reservoir, Stage I, on the Navidad River. This is a reservoir-and-outlet connection; exact gate positions, releases and present operating conditions are outside the naming finding.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Navidad and Lavaca receiving junction
correspondence.finding: Below the dam, the mapped Navidad River continues through the Palmetto Bend wetland setting into the lower receiving channel. The western Lavaca approach, intermediate wetland channels and the combined channel above and below the FM 616 crossing are visible. Lavaca River labels continue downstream. The reservoir profile separately identifies Navidad as a tributary of Lavaca. No precise point for the reach-name boundary is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Lavaca estuary and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The named Lavaca River continues south past the Menefee and Redfish waters and along the western side of Swan Lake to the river-mouth and adjoining bay. The official basin overview identifies its receiving water as Lavaca Bay. The actual selected endpoint is in that adjacent bay setting. The modeled final segment cuts across the mapped western mouth spit instead of tracing the longer channel around it, and other lower segments cut bends. The river, mapped outlet and receiving bay are visibly connected at ordinary estuary scale; no separate watercourse is claimed along the shortcut or a precise present shoreline.

correspondence.component_scope: Western small-water opening and northward feeder
correspondence.finding: The chosen western opening follows small waters and a northward stream into the southwestern side of the first large irregular lake. The map distinguishes the adjoining feeder branches. Neither a separate opening name nor the natural source of the entire river is established.

correspondence.component_scope: First large lake and eastern outlet
correspondence.finding: The route crosses the large irregular lake eastward and leaves by its eastern channel. The original identifies this lake with a numbered fish-resource symbol, whose margin describes unnamed lakes; that historical wording is not a finding that no current local name exists.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeastward connecting stream and small lakes
correspondence.finding: The eastern outlet turns southeast through connected smaller waters and stream reaches into the long middle lake. Northern and southern lateral waters are distinguishable from this through-going corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Long bent middle lake and eastern narrows
correspondence.finding: The selection traverses the long southeast-bending lake and its eastern narrows. The mapped outlet continues east before turning south; the nearby fish-resource and thematic boundary symbols are not hydronyms or connecting channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward outlet, broad middle lake and eastward continuation
correspondence.finding: The source depicts the southward connecting stream entering a broad lake, its southeastern arm, and the eastward outlet among smaller lakes. The selected route and lateral arrivals can be followed to the eastern Washburn sheet edge.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern northward bend and lake-side junction
correspondence.finding: Figure 7 continues the same middle lake succession beyond the sheet edge. It depicts the eastward link, short northern bend, and junction at the northern end of the elongated eastern lake, with a southeastward continuation distinct from its long southern arm.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southeastward stream and minor lake links
correspondence.finding: The figure shows the connected southeastward stream, small lake links and side-stream junctions leading to Jayco Lake’s northwestern approach. Its heavy enclosing line is the drainage-basin boundary, not the selected river.

correspondence.component_scope: Jayco Lake inlet, through-lake passage and southwestern outlet
correspondence.finding: The selected approach enters the northwestern side of the waterbody labelled Jayco Lake and crosses its connected lake waters to the southwestern outlet. Its lake identity remains distinct from the river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Jayco River outlet and Albert Edward Bay terminal
correspondence.finding: Figure 7 and its inset connect the lake outlet to the short Jayco River and Albert Edward Bay. The selected terminal lies in this coastal outlet setting. The adjacent Char/Fish Trap drainage has its own outlet, shown separately in Figure 8.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and initial northward feeder near El Topo
correspondence.finding: The Mexicali original depicts the initial small, unlabelled drainage near El Topo and its northward continuation to the western sheet edge. The separately labelled Arroyo San Pedro lies farther south and is not assigned to this selected opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Western turn through Piedras Finas, La Tortuga and Las Calabazas
correspondence.finding: The adjoining Tijuana original continues the mapped drainage through the Piedras Finas label, the westward valley by La Tortuga and the Las Calabazas corridor. The selected turning pattern and intervening joins correspond at ordinary regional scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Arroyo Las Palmas and Valle de las Palmas joins
correspondence.finding: The selected southwestern-to-northwestern course follows the labelled Arroyo Las Palmas through the valley and downstream turn toward the reservoir. Arroyo Seco approaches separately from the north; the selection uses the southern Las Palmas approach.

correspondence.component_scope: Presa Abelardo L. Rodríguez passage
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor enters the mapped Abelardo L. Rodríguez impoundment setting and continues through its narrowed northern end near Piedras Blancas. The source distinguishes waterbody, intermittent-water and dam symbols. This supports the reservoir passage without asserting present storage or operation.

correspondence.component_scope: Reservoir outlet through urban Tijuana toward the international boundary
correspondence.finding: The selected urban corridor is geographically visible, but the acquired Tijuana sheet does not continuously depict the required outlet-to-border watercourse through the built-up area. The USGSTopo view identifies Tijuana River entering the United States but does not establish the complete intervening Mexican urban link.

correspondence.component_scope: Entire western terminal fragment and selected coastal endpoint
correspondence.finding: The USGSTopo original depicts Tijuana River turning through the valley and estuary north of the international boundary before reaching the Pacific. The selected western fragment instead crosses border-side land south of that mapped course and meets a different coastal point. No mapped waterway establishes that selected continuation.
